about: Foundation's plan as a kanban. GitHub issues are where the team moves cards; this file is the local copy the app shows in Settings → Plan. `npm run plan:push` writes it to GitHub, `npm run plan:pull` reads the issues back. Columns: needs-you (waits on a person: a key, an install, a decision), backlog, next, doing, review (built, waiting to merge or to be checked by a person), done.

cards.title: Sections are grids within themselves: open one full-screen as its own grid
cards.body: Josh, 2026-11-11: "The individual sections are actually grids within themselves, so opening them up to fullscreen opens up a full other grid." Sections nest (SectionDoc.parent, SectionDoc.grid). Open (was Expand) takes the view into a section's own grid, with every grid tool, and a breadcrumb under the top bar (Esc goes up). A section of cards opens as one section; splitting or adding beside it makes it a grid of sections. On the board such a section shows its grid in miniature; double-click opens it there. Cards added to it go to its first section; removing it removes what's inside. Checked in the browser two levels deep, day and night (docs/evidence/2026-11-11_grids-in-sections/); test/levels.test.ts, test/nested-sections.test.ts, e2e/wheel.spec.ts. Open: wires across levels, agents' cursors inside nested sections, presentation into nested grids (SPEC §7).

cards.title: Images rest bare; a clear image can be inverted on dark
cards.body: Josh, 2026-11-10: "Images don't need borders until they are rolled over, and if it is a transparent image on a dark background there should be the option to invert it." Media cards have no paper, border or shadow at rest (no well behind a loaded clear image); a hairline and the resize corner come with the pointer. An image with see-through pixels offers ◐ Invert on dark at night; MediaDoc.invert is shared and applies only at night (invert + hue-rotate by --night-hard). Checked day and night in the browser.

cards.title: Night is greys and white, with yellow and orange for attention
cards.body: Josh, 2026-11-10: "The color pallete of dark mode should not use the neon blues and greens, but use white and grey-scale colors, with the eventual pops of orange or yellow." Night surfaces are graphite (#0f0f10 … #1f1f21), the accent and focus white, ok light grey, eyebrows grey, warn yellow, bad orange; on-fill turns dark at night. The paper shader's night is graphite with grey dots. Agents stay violet; data-viz and wire type tones are unchanged. Day is unchanged. #/design shows it (docs/evidence/2026-11-10_carry/12).

cards.title: Carry a card to another section, a new section, or another board
cards.body: Josh, 2026-11-10: "It doesn't look like I can actually drag items from one section to another, dragging should not only be able to be dragged to other boards but it should create new sections to be dropped in." A card dragged out of its section lifts into a copy that follows the pointer (lib/carry.ts): another section rings and takes it where it's let go; an empty cell or past an edge of the board makes a new section for it; another space's tab (or its spaces-pane row) sends it to that board, into a section named From <board> (server send_to_board: note text, cells, its file; machines, huddles and stages stay). Anywhere else it flies back. Checked in the browser on all four paths (docs/evidence/2026-11-10_carry/); apps/server/test/carry.test.ts (4). Not yet in the e2e suite, and not tried on a real trackpad.

cards.title: A port opened as a page shows its last load after the machine stops
cards.body: The page's frame isn't told the machine stopped. Show it as stopped (and reload when it starts again).

cards.title: Tokens for text on a solid fill and for highlights
cards.body: Most of the 19 raw colours left in components (`design.test.ts`'s allowlist) are white text on a solid state or person colour and the port bead's white gloss. A `--color-on-fill` and a highlight token in `tokens.css` would clear them; lower the test's ceiling as they go.

cards.title: Moving a huddle card while someone joins can drop who's in it
cards.body: Huddle state lives on the panel object; a move at the same moment overwrites it until the next join or leave. Keep it in its own map.

cards.title: The agent runtime starts an npm-installed claude.cmd safely
cards.body: `agent.ts` spawns `config.claudeCli` directly. That works while Claude Code is `claude.exe`, but an npm-installed `claude.cmd` can't be spawned without a shell. Reuse `claudeCommand` from `rea.ts` (found 2026-11-07 while fixing the REA job).

cards.title: Follow an agent
cards.body: Done 2026-11-07: Follow on any working agent's roster row; your view glides (at your zoom) to keep its cursor in the middle of the open paper, a pill says whom you're following with Stop, and it ends when you press, drag or wheel the grid, press Esc, or the agent leaves.

cards.title: Keys typed right after a tap of Space can reach the board's shortcuts
cards.body: A tap of Space opens the sheet for typing, but its field takes focus on the next animation frame. Letters typed in that gap go to the board (A toggles the agent layer), seen in a headless check on 2026-11-07. Focus the field in the same frame, and hold keys typed before it's ready.

cards.title: Read Vision Code's real address from server-runtime.json
cards.body: Vision moves to the next port when :3783 is taken, and records where it went in `<T3CODE_HOME>/userdata/server-runtime.json`. Default `T3_URL` from it instead of assuming :3783.

cards.title: Flowform sign-in attempts are lost on a server restart
cards.body: Attempts live in server memory for 10 minutes, so a `tsx watch` restart mid-sign-in makes the person click again. Keep them in SQLite.

cards.title: The REA job on Windows
cards.body: It spawns `npx` without a shell; Windows needs `npx.cmd` resolved safely (its arguments include a target). The REA runner and the Vision brief are also unexercised end to end.

cards.title: Notes and tables say which agent made them
cards.body: A real turn's cards are signed in the activity, but `createdBy` is set on panels only, so a note or table doesn't say which agent made it.

cards.title: A finished ask from the sheet leaves the roster with nowhere to find it
cards.body: Agents asked from the sheet run without a tab; their sessions are in the side pane, but nothing points there once the roster lets them go 2.4 s after they finish (SPEC §7).

cards.title: Opening the side pane beside a session on a narrow window leaves a sliver
cards.body: The floor only gives way on its own. Narrow the session instead when the pane is opened by hand.

cards.title: The crew driven by a real model
cards.body: Claude Code signed back in; three real subscription turns drove the crew on 2026-11-07 (`docs/evidence/2026-11-07_crew/` 10–14) and found five faults, fixed the same day: connectors hosting the new section, raw markdown tables, port ids in cursor labels, the helper's brief logged as the person's ask, section ids in activity.

cards.title: Publish the first desktop release to the org repo
cards.body: The update feed is a 404: no release was ever published, so an installed copy has nothing to update to. Decided 2026-11-12 (Josh): the feed lives on `Normal-AI-Vibe-Code/Foundation`; builds from here on ask it and `npm run release -- publish` targets it. What's left, and needs a person: (1) write access to that repo for whoever publishes (the `gh` account on Josh's PC has read only), and the release tag pushed there; (2) `npm run release -- bump <v>`, `build`, push the tag, `publish`; (3) install from that release on a second computer and watch it take the next one; (4) installed 0.3.0 copies still ask the fork: reinstall them once, or publish the first release to the fork too; (5) back up `~/.tauri/foundation-updater.key` and `.password` somewhere that isn't this PC. Also unrun: macOS, Linux, the MSI path; the Windows installer isn't code-signed.

cards.title: Decide the repo's visibility (public fork today)
cards.body: `joshleong/Foundation` is public and holds company plans and connector names (and now these issues). Make it private, or move it to the Form Industries org (SPEC §6 #1).

cards.title: The Slack board: a section per channel, live, kept by agents
cards.body: Josh, 2026-11-12: a board with a section for every Slack channel, each gathering the channel's latest images, top-level items and a summary, a live Slack mark on each section, and Foundation's agents pulling information, editing summaries and organizing images as they're posted. Built: slacklive.ts (the board, the `slack` server map, reading, images, the agent queue), POST /api/slack/events, apps/slack-agent (Slack's bolt-js-support-agent template plus foundation/bridge.js, `npm run slack`), the Slack mark on section headers and #/design, ⌘K → Open the Slack board. Agents are off until a person presses ✦. Checked against a stand-in Slack with the scripted agent: slacklive.test.ts, bridge.test.js, browser day and night (docs/evidence/2026-11-12_slack-board/). Waits on Josh: slack login and linking the project to app A0CGWUQ6WSK, FOUNDATION_SERVICE_TOKEN in .env, then a run against the real workspace and one real agent summary (SPEC, Waiting on a person).

cards.title: Create the Slack app and set SLACK_BOT_TOKEN
cards.body: Create the app from `docs/slack-app-manifest.yml`, install it, set `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` (and `SLACK_USER_TOKEN` for ⌘K search). Channel cards, links, huddle invites, Hermes DMs and `lay_out` from Slack have only run against a stand-in Slack (SPEC §6 #7).

cards.title: Keys: BomForm + CA, API credits, rea-agents setup
cards.body: `BOMFORM_MCP_URL` + `BOMFORM_API_KEY` + `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`, or the Data Room read token; `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` for the API runtime (untested); `npx rea-agents setup` before a reverse-engineering card's Run (SPEC §6).

cards.title: The Data Room's daily BomForm sync stopped on 2026-09-05
cards.body: BomForm reads the Data Room's copy, labelled "copy · 58d old". Check `BOMFORM_API_KEY` / `CRON_SECRET` on Vercel, merge `foundation-bomform-read` and point `DATAROOM_BOMFORM_URL` at airformdata.com (SPEC §6 #5).

cards.title: Machines on Kiri (Windows)
cards.body: Kiri installed by `npm run kiri:install` (MSI checked against a pinned SHA-256), started with `npm run dev`, woken by Start, and launched outside the server's process tree so it outlives Foundation. Still: Kiri's Windows installer is unsigned, and Kiri doesn't apply per-container memory/CPU caps.

cards.title: Issues on and the plan pushed to GitHub
cards.body: Done 2026-11-08 with Josh's go-ahead: issues turned on for `joshleong/Foundation` and `npm run plan:push` made one issue per card (labels `plan`, `kind:`, `status:`, `area:`, a milestone each; Done cards closed). Move cards on GitHub by their `status:` label, then `npm run plan:pull`.

cards.title: Give gh the project scope so the kanban can live in GitHub Projects
cards.body: Issues carry the board today (status labels + milestones). For a GitHub Projects board, run `gh auth refresh -s project,read:project` and then `npm run plan:project`, which makes the project and adds every open issue with its column.

cards.title: Remove the scratch "Foundation hand-offs" project from Vision Code
cards.body: Left behind when `npm test` used to reach the real Vision Code (fixed 2026-11-03). Delete it in Vision Code.

cards.title: See an export come back from a real Vision Code thread
cards.body: One real hand-off started a Supervised thread that read the brief and waited on approval. Approve its file writes in Vision Code and check the export lands beside the brief as a card, then that reviewers are asked (SPEC §3 Vision loop).

cards.title: Vision Code hand-offs on Windows
cards.body: Built 2026-11-07 (`t3paths.ts`): Vision Code's CLI and store are found on Windows and Linux, overrides still win, and when nothing is found the side pane and the hand-off card list every path tried. On this machine it found `C:\Dev\Vision\.tools\code-server	3.exe` and `%APPDATA%\co.normallab.vision\code` and read 4 threads. Left for a person: press Run on a hand-off card on Windows with Vision Code open, and approve the thread there.

cards.title: Release stage writes BOM lines to BomForm
cards.body: Release completes the stage but writes nothing. Once BomForm's write tools are keyed, write the chosen CAD's BOM lines, person-approved, and show what was written on the stage (SPEC §3 Design pipelines).

cards.title: A hosted Foundation reaches Vision Code by a pairing link
cards.body: Hand-offs use T3's CLI on the same machine. A hosted server needs a T3 pairing link and a stored client credential: a decision for Josh on where that credential lives (SPEC §7).

cards.title: Reviews come back as Vision's own verdict, not only asks
cards.body: Review asks each reviewer through Hermes. Vision has its own review tools; bring their verdict back onto the Review stage beside the people's answers.

cards.title: A person's table (⌘K) added into an app section hides behind the app
cards.body: Agents' cards no longer do this: since 2026-11-07 a card an agent adds to a hosted section makes the app a card in the flow beside it (`cardSection` in `tools.ts`). The client's own add paths (⌘K, the section toolbar, the empty-section actions) should do the same.

cards.title: The + add-section buttons in the gaps catch double-clicks
cards.body: The + buttons sit in the 40 px gaps between sections, so a double-click aimed at the gap adds a section. Make adding a single, deliberate press that a double-click can't trigger (SPEC §7).

cards.title: Wires between other sections stay bright over an expanded section's dimmed neighbours
cards.body: When a section is expanded its neighbours fade to 12 %, but the wires between them draw at full strength. Dim them with their sections (SPEC §7).

cards.title: Prune the legacy toolbar CSS and the last raw colours
cards.body: `.app-bar` is still in App.css; a few `rgba()` and hex colours and hover transitions on `background` remain and lag the night fade. Prune them and add a `check-design` test that ratchets raw colours down (Phase 1 leftover, DESIGN §2).

cards.title: Huddle recordings can't seek: Chrome's WebM has no duration
cards.body: MediaRecorder's WebM carries no duration, so the archive's player can't seek until it has played through. Write the duration into the file before it uploads (SPEC §7).

cards.title: A crew-wide stop
cards.body: Done 2026-11-07: **Stop all** heads the crew roster when two or more of yours are working, and ⌘K → Stop all my agents does the same. Server-side (`POST /api/agent/runs/stop-all`, `stopAllRuns`): every run of yours on this board, helpers included, and nobody else's.

cards.title: Agents that point at a cell or a port
cards.body: Done 2026-11-07: `point_at` aims an agent's cursor at a table cell ("D5") or a panel's port, with a laser ring on the spot; it writes nothing. The agent's prompt tells it to point as it explains. Seen on the scripted runtime: the laser sat on D5 (52.62). A real model hasn't used it yet.

cards.title: Helpers see the lead's plan and each other's work
cards.body: Done 2026-11-08: a helper's brief carries the lead's plan (`set_plan`) and what the crew has made so far, and `crew_work` (read) keeps it current: the ask, the plan, each agent's state, sections and cards, finished helpers included. On the script runtime, a second helper saw the first one's “Suppliers to call” and wrote only the lead times (`crew.test.ts`, `e2e/crew.spec.ts`). Not yet seen with a real model.

cards.title: Spatial voice: ask the agent nearest your pointer
cards.body: Holding Space near a working agent's cursor talks to that agent instead of starting a new one.

cards.title: A local transcriber so voice stays in-house
cards.body: Web Speech sends mic audio to the browser maker's service. Whisper on the server or Vision's `@pacific/voice` would keep it in-house, for the crew's sheet and huddle transcripts alike.

cards.title: Run npm run kiri:install on a Mac and on Linux
cards.body: `scripts/kiri.mjs` has run on Windows only. Its macOS (`.dmg`, `open -a Kiri`) and Linux (`.deb`/`.rpm`, `kiri daemon`) paths are written from Kiri's docs and not yet tried.

cards.title: The voice sheet opens the microphone twice
cards.body: The level meter's getUserMedia runs beside Web Speech: in the desktop app and some browsers that's a second permission prompt (SPEC §7).

cards.title: Measure Space's three jobs on a real trackpad
cards.body: Held still it listens after 240 ms, tapped it types, held with a drag it pans. Someone who holds Space and waits before dragging sees the sheet flash. Check with real people.

cards.title: A daily "what changed" digest note by the agent
cards.body: Done 2026-11-07: a server-built note (no model) in the company board's "Daily digest" section each morning: who did what, sections and cards added or removed, each connector compared with the last digest. One per day, 14 kept by reusing the oldest, `write_digest` for one now.

cards.title: BomForm snapshot cached and diffed
cards.body: Keep each day's BomForm snapshot and show what changed since the last one on the connector.

cards.title: Spoken conversations about the company (@pacific/voice)
cards.body: Vision's realtime voice session, pointed at the company board's tools.

cards.title: Semantic search: e5 text, SigLIP images, RRF k=60
cards.body: Port flowform's semantic search beside FTS5, fused by reciprocal rank. It would also let find_images see inside pictures (SPEC §7).

cards.title: Slack per-person OAuth, with visibility that fails closed
cards.body: Today ⌘K searches Slack with one user token. flowform's per-person OAuth and mirrored visibility are the target.

cards.title: Google Drive and Figma connectors
cards.body: Search and cards for Drive files and Figma frames.

cards.title: An app registry UI
cards.body: See and edit the company's apps (name, URL, repo, MCP, ports) instead of a list in code.

cards.title: foundation.json in our vibe-coded apps
cards.body: Publish `/.well-known/foundation.json` from each app so opening its URL gives it a name, ports, MCP and repo. Also exercises the postMessage bridge with a real app, which hasn't happened yet.

cards.title: Wires that call MCP tools on input
cards.body: A value arriving on a port calls an app's MCP tool and sends the result on.

cards.title: Agents run commands in a machine a person started, approved per command
cards.body: Agents can read a machine's last screen; let them propose a command that runs once a person approves it on the card.

cards.title: docker compose stacks as sections; noVNC and ttyd presets
cards.body: A compose file opens as a section of machines wired together; desktop presets for web desktops.

cards.title: A machine's terminal selection lands off at zooms other than 100 %
cards.body: xterm measures its cells unscaled, so a mouse selection is off by the zoom factor (and now by a section's fit). Typing is fine.

cards.title: Per-person recording opt-out
cards.body: Anyone can start recording and everyone sees REC, but nobody can stay out except by leaving.

cards.title: Slack live (Socket Mode), threads, and a summary at the end of a session
cards.body: Cards poll every 5 s; threads show a count but can't be opened; a session's summary could post when it ends, person-approved.

cards.title: Screen share into the portal; spatial audio while roaming
cards.body: Share a screen as a tile; voices fade with distance from the portal while you roam the board.

cards.title: An SFU past six people; TURN by default
cards.body: The mesh strains past about six. LiveKit self-hosted is the step up. Only STUN by default, so strict NATs need `FOUNDATION_ICE_SERVERS`.

cards.title: Inviting a channel to a new huddle waits 400 ms for the card to sync
cards.body: A server-side create-and-invite would remove the wait.

cards.title: Check speech transcription with a real voice
cards.body: Huddle transcripts and the crew's sheet were checked with typed lines and a stand-in recogniser. Talk in a huddle and to the sheet on a real machine.

cards.title: Live pages and section fit: the mount gate ignores the fit
cards.body: Frames mount when on screen and the camera's zoom is ≥ 0.3 (`useOnScreen`), whatever the section's fit. So a page fitted to 27 % in a section at 100 % zoom mounts at an effective 27 % (costly, unreadable), while one reported on the crowded company board stayed a poster (not reproduced: likely the board was zoomed out below 0.3). Decide the rule on the effective scale (zoom × fit) and reproduce the report first.

cards.title: A machine card's hover bar covers its port pills (a design call)
cards.body: Seen while checking machine pages (2026-11-07): the bar that drops in over a card's top edge on hover sits over the machine card's head, where its published ports are pills (`:8080 ↗`), so they're hard to press. Options: move the port pills to the card's foot (as the huddle card moved its controls to the bottom for the same reason); start the head below the bar's 30 px; or let the bar skip machine cards and put its actions in the foot. DESIGN puts the pills in the head today, so this is Josh's call.

cards.title: A person's tool calls are logged as an agent; grid edits aren't logged
cards.body: `touch()` in `tools.ts` logs every tool call with role `agent`, including a person's HTTP call, so the daily digest counts people as agents. A person's own edits on the grid write no activity at all. Log the actor's real role, and log a person's structural edits (sections and cards added or removed).

cards.title: Port what's still missing from the October grid branch
cards.body: `feat/grid-interactions-and-persistence` (2026-10-04, merged into the upstream org repo, not into this one) was written on the app before the monorepo: multi-select and merging sections, dragging a card across sections, media ingest, local persistence, a voice command bar and sound effects (`src/sound/sfx.ts`). It can't be merged (different layout and store); compare it with today's app and port the parts that are still missing.

cards.title: Notes in CodeMirror with y-codemirror
cards.body: Two people editing the very same word can interleave letters (each edit rebases as one change). A CodeMirror binding fixes that and brings syntax-aware editing; undo would last across reloads.

cards.title: Narrow the whole-store subscribers (GridViewport, WireLayer, MapView)
cards.body: They render on every change on a big board. Narrow them the way `useSection` did.

cards.title: Framing a section can put its tools off screen; an empty section's welcome reads small
cards.body: Framing zooms to a section's cards (about 0.55 at 1440×900). Frame tighter when it holds one card or none, and keep its top-right tools in view.

cards.title: Backward wires into a pipeline's first column hook tightly
cards.body: The input sits 28 px from the section's wall, leaving about 14 px for the U-turn. A wider left pad on pipeline sections gives it room.

cards.title: Wire landings collide at the far end of an edge
cards.body: Landings push apart along an edge but not at the far end, so two apps crowding one edge can tilt one wire. Also: a wire from a split app section can run tight along a neighbour's edge.

cards.title: An expanded section's size snaps while its card eases
cards.body: Wires jump to the new rects at once. Animate the store's rect so they travel together. Floating cards also stay where they were, which can make the open section wide.

cards.title: Tune throw momentum, MIN_FIT and pinch on a real trackpad
cards.body: Throws carry velocity × 125 ms; fitted cards stop shrinking at 40 %. Both are judgement calls made headless; tune with a person on a real display.

cards.title: Re-run the perf trace on a real GPU and decide on live frames during camera moves
cards.body: About 5 % of frames drop to 30 fps with live apps on screen in headless Chromium. Measure on the Mac and Windows GPUs, then choose: a still in their place while the camera moves, or live.

cards.title: Cards a tool changed without naming them go unringed
cards.body: Rings come from ids in tool inputs and results. Ring from the activity a run wrote instead.

cards.title: Stopping the launcher from outside leaves its children running (Windows)
cards.body: A hard kill of `scripts/dev.mjs` (an IDE stop button, Task Manager) never reaches its `taskkill /T`, so the server, Vite and the window keep their ports. Tie the children to the launcher.

cards.title: Keys say ⌘ on Windows
cards.body: Merged 2026-11-08 (`fix/shortcut-labels`): labels print ⌘ on a Mac and Ctrl on Windows and Linux through `lib/keys.ts`; key chips never wrap.

cards.title: A header-capable sync transport (ticket exchange)
cards.body: WebSocket auth uses the cookie, so a packaged app can't use a hosted server (cross-site). A short-lived ticket, like T3's `websocket-ticket`, fixes it.

cards.title: CI: tests, typecheck and Tauri builds on Windows, macOS and Linux
cards.body: `npm test`, typecheck and `cargo build` on every push, on windows-latest too. Then signed installers.

cards.title: A hosted server: S3 media, Postgres or libsql
cards.body: And what a hosted server means for machines (they'd run on the host) and Vision hand-offs (a pairing link).

cards.title: One UI package across Data Room, Creation, Vision and Foundation
cards.body: Panels from the Data Room, Creation and Vision sharing `@foundation/ui` (or Vision's `@pacific/ui` directly).

cards.title: Run and sign the desktop installers; rebuild macOS
cards.body: The Windows NSIS and MSI builds were made but never run, and nothing is signed. The macOS build wasn't rebuilt since the Windows work.

cards.title: Linking accounts and other admin as a screen
cards.body: Linking two users is `npm run link-accounts`. Admin (users, audit) has no UI yet.

cards.title: Panel iframes are sandboxed with allow-same-origin
cards.body: A hostile app on the same origin could escape. Serve third-party apps from their own origins and drop allow-same-origin where we can.

cards.title: Commit the flowform importer's fixture rooms
cards.body: `flowform-import.test.ts`'s six tests skip because the rooms were never committed (the old `data/` ignore caught them). Whoever has them should commit them.

cards.title: Refresh the app floorplan after this release
cards.body: `public/floorplan.html` is a snapshot from 2026-11-03; machines, the crew, section fit and the plan board came since (docs/floorplan.md).

cards.title: A connector shown as a card (not hosted) has no name at rest
cards.body: Cards have no title at rest by design; hosted apps and pipeline stages name themselves, but a connector card reads by its body only.

cards.title: The plan as a kanban: GitHub issues and Settings → Plan
cards.body: `docs/plan.json` is the plan; `npm run plan:push` / `plan:pull` keep it and GitHub issues in step; Settings → Plan shows it as a board, and admins move cards there. SPEC §8 points here instead of a phase table. Built and checked in the browser; waiting on the first push to GitHub (see "Turn on issues and push the plan to GitHub").

cards.title: The desktop app updates itself (signed feed, a card, one press)
cards.body: Like Vision (ADR-055): tauri-plugin-updater reads latest.json on the newest GitHub release, checks the installer against Foundation’s key, a person presses Update. npm run release builds and publishes. Checked on a real install (docs/evidence/2026-11-08_desktop-updates/).

cards.title: A new app icon: an F laid in masonry
cards.body: apps/client/assets/foundation-icon.svg; the desktop icons and the browser tab use it.

cards.title: Josh's icon: four panels on a grid, in place of the masonry F
cards.body: apps/client/assets/foundation-mark.svg is the drawing (white). The desktop icons and the browser tab are the white mark on a glass squircle (translucent navy, sheen, lit rim; no blue); in the app the mark is blue on paper and white on fills. Shown on #/design → The mark, day and night (docs/evidence/2026-11-10_icon/). The installed app shows it after the next release build.

cards.title: Search inside documents; paste, folders and one upload tray
cards.body: PDF, Word, PowerPoint, Excel and OpenDocument files are read after their upload answers (a worker thread, capped per file; unpdf for PDF, a built-in zip + XML reader for the rest), kept by content and put into search; older files are read at boot. ⌘K and the search pane show the matching words, marked. On the grid: paste files or a screenshot where the pointer is, drop whole folders (laid out as a group under a note naming them), and every upload goes through one glass tray (three at a time, Retry on failure). Checked: `test/files-text.test.ts` (9), `e2e/files.spec.ts` (4), `#/design` → Adding files, day and night (`docs/evidence/2026-11-08_files-search/`). Open: scanned PDFs (no OCR), legacy .doc/.ppt/.xls, a real OS folder drag (the e2e walks a stand-in entry tree).

cards.title: An open section keeps its floating cards where they were
cards.body: Left over from #68 (the wires now travel with the card). A card dropped far right in the fitted view stays there when the section opens, so the open section is wide and the camera frames it smaller. Docked cards reflow; floating ones could be brought within the open width, or the open width could ignore outliers.

cards.title: Panel edges: a hairline and a clean cut, not a fade
cards.body: Josh, 2026-11-09: the left and right panels shouldn't fade the edge; a line, like a VS Code panel that resizes. The cards are clipped at the pane, each pane's edge is a hairline that turns blue under the pointer and drags to resize. Checked in the browser day and night (`docs/evidence/2026-11-09_edges-places-flowform/`).

cards.title: Places: approved folders on this computer, browsed and dragged from
cards.body: Settings → Places approves a folder (admins, as a person). The search pane's This computer chip browses it; a file dragged out is copied into the archive and lands as a card. Agents get `places` and `bring_file`. Read-only, nothing outside a place, secrets left where they are (`test/places.test.ts`). To check: a real folder on Josh's machine, a real model using the tools.

cards.title: Flowform link: read your boards and files through its MCP endpoint
cards.body: `flowformlink.ts`: OAuth (PKCE) to flowform-server's `/mcp`, `search:read canvas:read` only, tokens encrypted at rest; Connect/Disconnect in Settings → Services; agents get `flowform`. Registers afresh on every Connect (Flowform forgot a day-old registration). Josh connected it on 2026-11-11: 12 read tools, his 6 rooms, file search, all answered live (`docs/evidence/2026-11-11_flowform-live/`).

cards.title: Connect Flowform once, in Settings → Services
cards.body: Josh connected Flowform on 2026-11-11 (after the registration fix). Each person connects their own.

cards.title: Flowform's files in the search pane, to drag onto a board
cards.body: Search → Flowform: type and it searches your Flowform files through the link (Flowform's own `search`: uploads, board media, Slack, Figma); drag one out and it lands as a link card (Slack, Figma) or a note naming it. Checked in the browser against Josh's real files. The bytes don't come through: see `flowform-file-bytes`.

cards.title: Pull a Flowform board in from the app, and keep it in step
cards.body: Search → Flowform lists your rooms; press one and it lands as board `ff-<room>` (the importer's ids and ledger): a section per surface, notes, tables with cells, app and link cards at their Flowform positions; read again every 5 minutes and on ↻; edits and removals here stand, nothing deleted; a Flowform viewer can't bring one in. `flowform-live.ts`, `test/flowform-live.test.ts` (5); Form Industries (57 cards) brought in on a throwaway copy, day and night. Images, videos, files and Flowform's older tables arrive as named notes. To do: Josh brings his rooms into his own Foundation.

cards.title: Flowform file downloads, through the person's kept Flowform session
cards.body: Josh chose to keep the Flowform session for downloads (2026-11-11) and signed in through Flowform. Against production: Form Industries' 27 images and 4 videos (158 MB) and MatterForm's images, video and STEP file came into the archive and their cards became them. Flowform's file route needs `x-flowform-client-version` ≥ 1.9.0; renditions source → playback → display.

cards.title: The desktop app starts its own server
cards.body: The installed app expects a server at http://localhost:4410 and starts none, so on its own nothing in it connects (2026-11-09). Bundle the server (a Node sidecar with FTS5, or a single executable) and start it with the window, on a port outside Windows' reserved ranges; keep `Server` on the sign-in page for a hosted one.

cards.title: Upgrade Node on the Windows machine to 22.16 or newer
cards.body: System Node is 22.13.1 (no FTS5 in node:sqlite): the server can't start on it, which is why agents, Claude and data sources all failed to fetch. `winget install OpenJS.NodeJS.LTS`, then a new terminal. The launcher now says this itself.

cards.title: A heavy board holds 60 fps: picture levels, live pages and videos start when the camera is calm
cards.body: Josh, 2026-11-11, on a Flowform room with 27 photos (up to 4096 px, 110 MB), 4 videos and 15 live apps: "strive for 30-60 FPS". Pictures draw from the smallest of 256/512/1024/2048 px levels that's sharp at their drawn size, made once in a worker and kept in Cache Storage (`lib/imageLod.ts`); live pages and videos mount only once the camera is still, one at a time (`lib/calm.ts`); videos let go 5 s off screen. Measured by `e2e/heavy.spec.ts` (PERF_GPU=1) on the room's own geometry: SPEC §5.

cards.title: No card takes the wheel: Ctrl-click to use one, Ctrl+Enter full screen
cards.body: Josh, 2026-11-11: "Don't allow any of the objects to take over scroll, give them a ctrl keyboard command to interact with them, and allow them to be fullscreened". The wheel pans the grid over apps, maps, terminals and lists; ⌘/Ctrl-click puts a card in use; ⌘↵ / Ctrl+Enter or ⤢ opens it full screen without reloading it (`lib/cardUse.ts`, `e2e/card-use.spec.ts`).

cards.title: Make picture levels on the server, so a first visit never downloads an original
cards.body: Levels are made in the browser from the original, once per device (`lib/imageLod.ts`), so the first visit to a heavy board still downloads every original (110 MB on the Flowform room). The server has no image decoder; one (sharp, or a WASM decoder) would let it serve `/files/<id>?w=512` and share levels across devices.

cards.title: Out of search, into the hand: results you pick up, and a clipboard to carry several
cards.body: Josh, 2026-11-12: "a high physicality clipboard like experience where you can drag things from the search into Foundation". A result pulled out of search is a card in the hand (the picture, or a slip of paper): drag spring, lifted 2.5 %, leaning ≤ 2.5° about where it was pressed, its row kept behind it, the section under it ringing. It lands where it's let go; a file that has to be fetched waits at that spot on the board, then becomes the card; elsewhere or Esc it flies back. The clipboard at the pane's foot holds what you clip (＋, Ctrl-click, or a drop): pull one off, or the handle to carry the whole stack, fanned and trailing, dealt a step apart. `lib/pickup.ts`, `lib/pickupMath.ts`, `lib/hits.ts`, `state/clipboard.ts`, `shell/Clipboard.tsx`; `test/pickup.test.ts`; `#/design`. Checked in the browser, day and night (docs/evidence/2026-11-12_pickup-updates/). Open: Playwright doesn't drive it; trackpad and the packaged window untried; the held card isn't the landing size; ⌘C/⌘V not wired.

cards.title: Flowform's files in the one search, with pictures, and a room's files without bringing it in
cards.body: Josh, 2026-11-12: "read the same things as flowform in terms of the files that it has access too". The pane's search and ⌘K ask Flowform as the person (its own `search`: uploads, board media, Slack, Figma). Image and video results carry Flowform's own thumbnail (`/files/flowform/<file>/<rev>/thumb`, fetched as the person with the kept session). › on a room lists the files on its surfaces to pull out one at a time. `flowform-live.ts` (`searchFlowformFiles`, `roomFiles`), `flowformfiles.ts` (`fileThumb`); `test/flowformfiles.test.ts` (8). Checked against a stand-in only: the first run against server.formresearch.ai is Josh's (his link and session weren't borrowed).

cards.title: A server can name the oldest client it still works with
cards.body: From reading Flowform's updater (2026-11-12): its server refuses clients under a minimum. `FOUNDATION_MIN_CLIENT=x.y.z`: `/auth/config` carries it; an older client's socket ticket is refused (426) and its sync socket closed (4426); its update card stays up as needed, with Update and restart alone. `apps/server/src/clientversion.ts`, `packages/protocol/src/version.ts`, `update/updater.ts` (`learnMinimum`). `test/clientversion.test.ts` (5, real sockets), `test/update.test.ts` (8). Seen in the browser against a server set to 0.9.0. The installed-app path (meet a minimum, update through it) is unrun until a release is published (publish-first-release).

cards.title: An agent group on every section, and the agents pane
cards.body: Built 2026-11-12: a tab right above each section with a face per agent at work inside it (hover, or pinned on this device; at screen size at any zoom; it comes down with the view when the section fills it). A free agent joins the group of the section it aims into and leaves when it moves on. A lead and its helpers read as one team. It opens into the agents pane on the right (✦ in the top bar too): every agent by section, what it's doing, who works with whom, Follow / Open / Stop. `components/SectionCrew.tsx`, `shell/AgentsPane.tsx`, `lib/sectionCrew.ts`, `lib/crewWatch.ts`. `test/section-crew.test.ts` (8), `e2e/section-crew.spec.ts` (3, two people, script runtime), `docs/evidence/2026-11-12_section-agents/`. To check: with a real model turn; whether the tab's place and the pin feel right (Josh).

cards.title: Agents in the section, a text box, and a fuller right-click menu
cards.body: Built 2026-11-13 (Josh: "bring the agent view into the sections … make apparent the ability to have agents collaborate and build things in the interface with the user … a formatted word text box that is a WYSIWYG editor"). At rest every section's header carries ✦ Agents (it counts the agents at work) and ⤢, the way into its own grid. The chip opens the section's agents in its corner: who is at work, what agents made there, and a composer that asks an agent to build in that section; Keep here puts it on the board as a card (`panel: "crew"`). A text box is a note written as formatted text with a toolbar, kept as the note's markdown in the same shared text (`NoteDoc.rich`; `add_note` takes `text_box`). The right-click menu leads with asking an agent and groups Add / Live / Sections. `components/SectionAgents.tsx`, `components/RichText.tsx`, `components/sectionMenu.ts`. `e2e/section-agents.spec.ts` (5, two people, script runtime), `docs/evidence/2026-11-13_agents-in-sections/`. To check: a real model turn asked from the panel; a viewer; under Rune (no chip at rest there); whether the marks at rest are the right weight (Josh).

cards.title: Decide: what lets a posted agent keep working (sign-in is decided)
cards.body: **Sign-in inside a machine: decided (Josh, 2026-11-12).** Offer both, the subscription first, and keep them apart as separate instances of Claude. (a) A Claude folder on this computer, signed in to a subscription, mounted into the machine ("Mount ~/.claude"). (b) A token or key, passed in only when a run starts. A machine's agent uses (a) when there is one and (b) otherwise, unless a person picks. Each is its own Claude instance: its own folder, sign-in, history and name in Settings, never two sharing one folder. Found the same day: `~/.claude` here is 2.1 GB and holds every project's transcripts and history beside `.credentials.json`, so the default is a folder of its own per instance (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`), signed in once by a person; mounting the whole of `~/.claude` stays a choice a person makes on the card, said plainly. It breaks no-host-mounts for that one folder only. Untested: Docker and Kiri were both stopped, so no mount has been tried on either. **Still open:** the invariant says nothing that spends money or runs code starts without a person. Is posting an agent to a section, from a browser session, the consent for it to keep working inside that section and its machine until someone pauses it (recommended), or does every turn need a press?

cards.title: Agents posted to a section: they stay in its group, with a brief and a subscription
cards.body: Today a section's group is whoever aims there now (section-agents). A person posts an agent to a section: a name, a brief, the Claude subscription or key it runs on, and what it's bound to (the section's cards, a machine, an app and its GitHub repo). Stored on the board, so its face stays in the group when idle, marked as resident, not visiting; free agents still come and go. Settings → Services lists the subscriptions. Needs agent-consent-and-tokens.

cards.title: Claude Code agents that run inside a machine (Kiri or Docker)
cards.body: A machine image with Claude Code installed and a repo cloned inside; the server runs `claude -p --output-format stream-json` in it through the Engine API exec, with Foundation's MCP tools attached, and streams it into the session view. Each one is a new instance with its own disk, started by a person. Sign-in (decided 2026-11-12, #122): the machine's card offers both, a Claude folder signed in to a subscription (mounted) first, then a token or key; each is a separate Claude instance with its own folder. Settings → Services lists the instances. Kiri's containers share one small VM (WSL 2 on Windows): they separate our own agents, they don't contain hostile code. To find out first: whether Kiri and Docker Desktop both bind a Windows folder into a machine, and whether Claude Code in Linux reads a sign-in made on Windows. Posted agents (posted-agents) wait on the consent call in #122.

cards.title: Foundation's own T3 instance, and this computer's agents in the pane
cards.body: Built 2026-11-12 (Josh: build off Vision's T3, a T3 instance running in Foundation that the agent panel reads). `apps/server/src/t3host.ts` starts the unmodified `t3` 0.0.44 in `<data>/t3` the way Vision does (bootstrap on stdin, token exchange, socket ticket), person-started only, and keeps its providers and threads; `/api/t3host`; the agents pane's foot lists each agent with how it stands and its threads at work. `test/t3host.test.ts` (7, stand-in t3), the real `t3.exe` on this PC (Claude ready on the Team subscription, Codex not installed, four off), `e2e/section-crew.spec.ts` (+2). To check: Start T3 from the pane on the real server (the system Node can't run it yet: node-upgrade-windows).

cards.title: A second renderer: Rune draws the board beside the web renderer
cards.body: Josh, 2026-11-12: a GPU-rendered interface (github.com/anomalyco/rune) side by side with the web UI, a toggle in Settings, boards marked as rendered by Rune, the web renderer untouched. Built as a first slice: `apps/rune` (Rust → wasm, WebGPU), `apps/client/src/rune` (the scene, the host, Settings → Renderer and its parity ledger, the mark in the bottom bar), `npm run rune:build`. Off by default. One camera and one store for both engines. Rune draws sections, notes (with its own text field for writing) and images; web content stays live as islands (#129). Checked headed on the GPU in Edge (`e2e/rune.spec.ts`, 6) and in `test/rune-scene.test.ts` (8); evidence in `docs/evidence/2026-11-12_rune/`. To check by hand: Settings → Renderer → Rune, then the company board; and `npm run desktop` with Rune on, which is unrun.

cards.title: Kimi and DeepSeek in T3, cloud and local: built; needs keys and a local model server to prove
cards.body: Built 2026-11-12: an admin adds Kimi or DeepSeek from the agents pane, in the cloud (the vendor's Anthropic-compatible address and an API key that goes straight to T3) or on this computer (a local model server, Ollama's address by default, no key); the pane keeps the two groups apart. Each is a Claude-driven T3 instance with its own Claude folder. Checked against a stand-in T3, and the real t3.exe took both instances with a made-up key. Needs Josh: (1) a Moonshot key and a DeepSeek key, typed into the form, then one ask to each: the default model ids (`kimi-k3`, `deepseek-v4-pro`) and addresses are from the vendors' pages and guides, not from a run. (2) For local: install Ollama 0.14 or newer and pull a model this PC can run (a DeepSeek R1 distill; Kimi's open weights are too large), then add it as local. (3) Codex (OpenAI): install `codex` and `codex login`; it then shows ready with no change here.

cards.title: Start a thread on a chosen agent from a section, and show it in that section's group
cards.body: Built 2026-11-12: Ask on a ready agent in the agents pane starts a supervised thread on it in Foundation's T3 for the section in use; the agent joins that section's group under its own name and follows its thread; Open (T3's own page) and Stop on its row. `apps/server/src/t3threads.ts`, `/api/t3host/threads`. `test/t3threads.test.ts` (10), `e2e/section-crew.spec.ts` against a stand-in T3. To check (Josh): Start T3, ask Claude something in a section on the real server. That spends a turn on the Team plan, so no agent has done it. Left: a thread can't write the board (t3-threads-write-the-board); approvals are answered in T3's page, not on the card.

cards.title: Rune: live cards as web islands over its canvas, and tables drawn by Rune
cards.body: Built 2026-11-12 (second slice). Apps, pages, machines, huddles, Slack, connectors, files, maps and video are the web's own components, placed over Rune's canvas as islands in a shell of their section (`src/rune/RuneIslands.tsx`; `scene.ts` `isIsland` decides, so each card is one engine's). A table is Rune's at rest (header, heads, ruling, what each cell shows) and the web's live sheet while it's the card in hand. Checked in `e2e/rune.spec.ts` (islands within 1 px of the store's rects; a table Rune → web → a formula typed → Rune) and `test/rune-scene.test.ts`. Left for later: cells edited in Rune's own field (so the first press lands on a cell), a table's wire handle at rest, islands under Rune's cards, and use / full screen checked under Rune.

cards.title: Rune: section tools, menu, drag, rename and Open; a card's hover bar, resize and carry
cards.body: Built 2026-11-13 (third slice). In Rune: a section's toolbar on hover (the web's list, `src/rune/tools.ts`, with line icons Rune draws), rename in Rune's own field, drag by the header to a cell or past an edge (its cards and islands travel with it; the landing cell rings), remove behind its confirmation, n more · Expand, Open as its own grid; the right-click menu is the web section's list, now shared (`components/sectionMenu.ts`); a note's bar (float or dock, remove) and resize corner, an image's remove and corner. Checked in `e2e/rune.spec.ts` (the eighth check) and `test/rune-scene.test.ts`. Left: carrying a card to another section or tab (lib/carry.ts's rules, with the lean), the gutters, + in the gaps, the empty section's welcome and file drops, a grid section's miniature, roll-over labels, tools that stay while the pointer is on a card, the settle ease after a drag.

cards.title: Rune: Hanken Grotesk, the paper's dots and grain, markdown, frame times, and the desktop build
cards.body: Built 2026-11-13 (fourth slice). The paper is the web paper's own shader inside Rune's frame (`apps/rune/src/paper.rs`, the compositor hook: grain, dots, pointer light, vignette, night; a section's dots too), since Rune's web canvas can't be see-through. Hanken Grotesk is handed to Rune as TrueType (`apps/rune/fonts`, from `scripts/rune-fonts.py`). A note's markdown is rendered by Rune's kit with the web note's margins. `build:desktop` runs `rune:build` (and goes on without it where there's no Rust toolchain). Frame times are measured (`e2e/rune-frames.spec.ts`, `docs/evidence/2026-11-13_rune-frames/`): Rune is slower than the web renderer on 300 notes and level on the heavy board. Checked in `e2e/rune.spec.ts` (the ninth check). Left: the installed app with Rune on (Windows, macOS, Linux's fallback), Cyrillic and Vietnamese, and the speed itself (its own card).

cards.title: Rune: hold 60 fps on a board of notes (it is slower than the web renderer there)
cards.body: Measured 2026-11-13 (`docs/evidence/2026-11-13_rune-frames/`): on 300 markdown notes the web renderer holds 60 fps and Rune runs long frames on a third to a half of them (p95 83 to 150 ms). Find what makes Rune's view run again on live-only frames (about one run per camera step and per grain tick: its `CommitWhy`), keep off-screen cards out of the frame (cull in `scene.ts`, or a cache that holds), and cut or throttle Rune's accessibility mirror (12 % of a pan). Done when `e2e/rune-frames.spec.ts` shows Rune at the web renderer's p95 on 300 notes, and then holds it there.

cards.title: An agent asked through T3 can read and write the board
cards.body: Built 2026-11-13: each ask has its own folder with a tool file (Foundation's tool server as that ask's crew member, board and an agent session for the asker); Foundation puts `--mcp-config .foundation-mcp.json --allowedTools mcp__foundation --strict-mcp-config` on each Claude-driven agent's launch line in its T3; the brief gives the agent the board and tells it to work on cards in its section; the pass ends with the thread. `test/t3threads.test.ts` (12); the real t3.exe took the launch line and kept Claude ready; in the browser a stand-in T3 used the pass and its card landed in the section as Claude's. To check (Josh): ask Claude through T3 on the real server for a card in a section (one turn on the Team plan). Left: approvals answered on the card (`thread.approval.respond`), presence across a restart of Foundation's server, moving the crew's own Claude runs onto T3 so there's one list, tools for Codex.

cards.title: A mention and owner index, so Today doesn't read every board
cards.body: Today reads every board on each load to find mentions, stages and changes. Fine for a handful of boards; past a few dozen it wants an index kept as boards change.

cards.title: The Shiba speaks its replies
cards.body: Replies are type only. The browser's speech synthesis (local on macOS) or Vision's `@pacific/voice` (paid, consented per talk, as in HomeForm).

cards.title: A profile form and the Shiba's first-run walkthrough
cards.body: Title, team and the words for "your work" are set only by telling the Shiba today. A small form on Today, and the Shiba asking a new person's role on their first visit.

cards.title: People's projects and goals from the Data Room on Today
cards.body: Needs a read endpoint in AirformDataRoom (proposed: `GET /api/foundation/goals?email=`, bearer `FOUNDATION_READ_TOKEN`, like the BomForm digest), then `DATAROOM_GOALS_URL` here (SPEC §6 #19).

cards.title: Set BomForm's, HyperForm's and FleetForm's addresses
cards.body: Today shows them as not linked until `BOMFORM_URL`, `HYPERFORM_URL`, `FLEETFORM_URL` are set (SPEC §6 #18). What is HyperForm's app? Only the Data Room's diligence video mentions it.

cards.title: Publish Foundation for Chrome to everyone
cards.body: The package, listing, images and policies are ready (`apps/extension/README.md`, `STORE.md`, `store/`, `npm run release -w @foundation/extension`). Needs a person: confirm the placeholders in `apps/extension/release.json` (hosted address, domains, support email, privacy URL), register a Chrome Web Store developer account under a company Google account (one-time fee), upload as Private to the Workspace domain, then a Workspace admin force-installs it by id with `dist/policy/admin-console-policy.json` (SPEC §6 #17).

cards.title: Load Foundation for Chrome in a real Chrome
cards.body: Checked in a real Chromium on 2026-11-11 (`apps/client/e2e/extension.spec.ts`): a new tab goes through the extension to Today, signed in; the popup reads `/api/today` from the extension's origin with Foundation's cookie; signed out it says so. Evidence: `docs/evidence/2026-11-11_chrome-extension/`. Branded Chrome with a hosted Foundation comes with the rollout (#110).

cards.title: Today and the Shiba: home before the boards
cards.body: Signed in, a person lands on Today: the Shiba (Vision's ethereal shiba as the agent's face) answers about their day and changes their goals; beside it what wants them (asks, @mentions, stages they own, files and changes on their boards, work matching their job), their goals and every company app. Evidence: `docs/evidence/2026-11-11_today-shiba/` (SPEC §0.2).
